newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ new dwelling trend up 1.0 pct from May to June.
newsitem.headline: NZ new dwelling trend up 1.0 pct from May to June.

text.p: Provisional building consent statistics for June 1997 show that the short-term trend estimate for the number of new dwelling unit authorisations continues the pattern of steady increases apparent since October, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
"This period of growth follows three years of large variation in dwelling consent statistics," SNZ said.
It said the trend estimate increased by 1.0 percent from May to June 1997, in line with the lack of fluctuation shown since September 1996.
"Since October 1996, the monthly trend movement has remained between 1.0 and 1.6 percent, apart from a 0.5 percent increase in May," SNZ said.
An estimated 1,944 new dwelling units were authorised for construction in June 1997, 15.4 percent more than in June 1996.
"This increase is large but is due to a very low value in June 1996 which accentuates the movement to the high June 1997 figure," SNZ said.

The largest increases in new dwelling consents from June 1996 to June 1997 were for Wellington city, which rose to 148 from 78; Rodney District, up to 86 from 58; North Shore City, up to 130 from 102; and Tauranga District, up to 159 from 131.
